intro.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that demonstrates server-side rendering (SSR) concepts, similar to the principles behind React Server Components and static site generation (SSG). You'll learn how to create components that can be pre-rendered on the server for faster initial page loads and better SEO. The core programming concept involves using Angular's built-in tools for SSR and understanding the differences between server-side and client-side rendering. You'll work with Angular components, TypeScript, and the Angular CLI to set up and configure rendering modes, focusing on when to use SSR versus SSG for optimal performance.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building high-performance, SEO-friendly web applications like e-commerce product pages, news websites, and content-heavy dashboards. For example, a product listing page uses SSR to render initial product cards and prices quickly for search engines, while interactive filters and 'Add to Cart' buttons are handled client-side. Similarly, a news article page might use SSG to pre-render static content for fast loading, with dynamic elements like live comment sections or personalized recommendations loaded separately. Understanding when to use server-side rendering, static generation, or client components helps developers optimize performance and user experience in real-world applications.
